name: EASTGROUP PROPERTIES, INC.
share_adj_basis: applied to revenue components only (v5.4); OE/share CAGR enters unadjusted

overrides_applied.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-11, accession 0000049600-26-000010), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Capital improvements' (us-gaap PaymentsForCapitalImprovements): $(51,116) thousand for FY2023, $(59,288) thousand for FY2024 and $(75,830) thousand for FY2025; the override value is the median of the three filed years (the FY2024 figure). Cross-checked against statements.json, whose capex series is exactly this line.
overrides_applied.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2025 under every candidate tag the engine reads, because in the FY2025 10-K EastGroup stopped filing PaymentsForConstructionInProcess (the minor tag the engine read for FY2022-24, whose FY2024 fact is a signed construction-payables change of -$17,170,000, not capex). The filer's recurring real-estate capex is the cash-flow line 'Capital improvements' (us-gaap PaymentsForCapitalImprovements), which statements.py reads as the capex series ($51,116,000 FY2023 / $59,288,000 FY2024 / $75,830,000 FY2025) but which is not in the engine's candidate tag list — the same dead end documented for MAA, AMH, ELS and others in this sweep. The engine applies this single value to every missing period (FY2025 and the assumed-zero years); filed values are never replaced, so FY2023 ($12,163,000) and FY2024 (-$17,170,000) in the base window still carry the wrong minor tag — disclosed, not hidden: the median of the three window years under the fill is the corrected FY2025 year, so the normalized base is the corrected figure (see analysis.md). Against the true per-year capital-improvements figures the single value overstates FY2025 capex charge by $0 in the median construction (it IS the FY2024 figure) and understates FY2025's filed $75,830,000 by $16,542,000 (flatters the latest year — stated here; the TTM pin charges the same $59,288,000, also below the FY2025 run rate, so the base is if anything generous on capex). Excluded, deliberately: 'Development of real estate' ($321,934,000 FY2025) and 'Acquisition of real estate' ($143,099,000 FY2025) are growth investment presented separately by the filer; charging them as capex would double-count growth the portfolio expansion already paid for (same treatment as AMH/AHR in this sweep).

fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 7.3%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md

CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED: the only cash tag filed for the latest fiscal year is the combined cash + restricted-cash total and no restricted-cash tag separates it — net debt is UNDERSTATED by the restricted amount (escrow / collateral / regulatory); check the balance sheet before trusting HIGH_NET_DEBT's absence
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Real Estate sector — OE/capex DCF fits real estate names poorly; grade confidence low

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-11, accession 0000049600-26-000010), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Capital improvements' (us-gaap PaymentsForCapitalImprovements): $(51,116) thousand for FY2023, $(59,288) thousand for FY2024 and $(75,830) thousand for FY2025; the override value is the median of the three filed years (the FY2024 figure). Cross-checked against statements.json, whose capex series is exactly this line.); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact

override_impact.basis: engine-native normalized base (median of last 3 FY) and weighted IRR, DCF run both ways (zero-fill baseline vs with-override); a --base-oe-ps TTM base is excluded from both sides — its override effect shows in ttm.py output
